newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-OPENER POCOCK GETS NZ TEST CALL-UP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-OPENER POCOCK GETS NZ TEST CALL-UP.

text.p: New Zealand's selectors named two spinners and brought in opener Blair Pocock on Thursday to their 12-man squad to face England in the first cricket test in Auckland.
Pocock, who earlier scored 43 for a New Zealand Selection XI against the tourists, was preferred to Craig Spearman as opening partner for Bryan Young.
The selectors kept plenty of bowling options open by including two spinners, Mark Haslam and Dipak Patel, as well as a trio of all-rounders in Chris Cairns, Nathan Astle and Justin Vaughan.
Selector Mike Shrimpton said the naming of Haslam and Patel was an "insurance policy" on a wicket that may take spin.
Coach Steve Rixon said England's victory by an innings over the Selection XI was a reminder of the visitors' strengths.

"I know how good the Englishmen can be, and today was a fair indication that they're pretty hungry for victory, so we've got to get our act together and play good cricket to make sure we beat them," he said.
The first test starts in Auckland on January 24.
Blair Pocock, Bryan Young, Adam Parore, Stephen Fleming, Nathan Astle, Chris Cairns, Lee Germon (captain), Mark Haslam, Dipak Patel, Simon Doull, Danny Morrison, Justin Vaughan.
